html:
The Illinois Confederation, or Illiniwek, was a group of about a dozen Algonquian tribes in the upper Mississippi valley, mostly in what is now the state of Illinois. Among them were the Kaskaskia, Peoria, Cahokia, Tamaroa and Michigamea.

They spoke Miami-Illinois, the same language as the Miami. They lived in large summer villages, farming maize, and went out to hunt bison on the prairies in winter.

In 1673 Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet visited them, and the Illinois became close allies of New France. French missions and the town of Kaskaskia grew among them. But the Haudenosaunee attacked them during the Beaver Wars, and war and disease cut their numbers sharply in the 1700s. The great mound site of Cahokia takes its name from one of their tribes, who lived there long after the mound builders. Their descendants are the Peoria Tribe of Oklahoma.
